items.title: Tesla says ‘Robotaxi’ is expanding — its own chart shows it’s not
items.topic: Tesla says ‘Robotaxi’ is expanding — its own chart shows it’s not
items.summary: Tesla's 'Robotaxi' program expansion claims are contradicted by its own data, showing no significant growth. The company's Full Self-Driving (FSD) beta program has faced challenges, with the number of active vehicles remaining stagnant. This discrepancy highlights the ongoing difficulties in deploying autonomous vehicles at scale.

items.title: Tesla’s robotaxi promises are clashing with reality
items.topic: Tesla’s robotaxi promises are clashing with reality
items.summary: Tesla's robotaxi promises are clashing with reality, as the company faces significant challenges in deploying its autonomous vehicles. Despite initial ambitious goals, the Full Self-Driving (FSD) beta program has seen limited progress, with safety concerns and regulatory hurdles slowing down the rollout. This highlights the gap between Tesla's vision and the practical realities of AV deployment.

items.title: Tesla’s robotaxis are moving in reverse
items.topic: Tesla’s robotaxis are moving in reverse
items.summary: Tesla's robotaxi program is reportedly moving in reverse, with the company facing setbacks in its Full Self-Driving (FSD) beta program. The number of active FSD-equipped vehicles has not increased as expected, and safety concerns have led to a more cautious approach. This development underscores the challenges in achieving widespread autonomous vehicle deployment.

items.title: Tesla ‘Full Self-Driving’ got me a speeding ticket, and Tesla killed the fix
items.topic: Tesla ‘Full Self-Driving’ got me a speeding ticket, and Tesla killed the fix
items.summary: A Tesla owner reported receiving a speeding ticket while using the Full Self-Driving (FSD) beta feature. Tesla subsequently disabled the feature that allowed the vehicle to exceed speed limits, but the fix has not been re-enabled. This incident highlights the ongoing safety and regulatory issues with FSD and the need for more robust oversight.

items.title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.topic: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.summary: The arXiv paper introduces CommandLM, a multimodal large language model that generates human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles from fused multi-sensor data, achieving CIDEr 0.67 and BERT-F1 0.88 on the CommandLM-nuScenes dataset. CommandLM processes temporally fused bird's-eye view representations from LiDAR and multi-camera inputs via a Q-Former adapter connected to a quantized, LoRA-fine-tuned large language model. This model is essential for safety, trust, and regulation in autonomous driving systems. The CommandLM-nuScenes dataset is used to train CommandLM, which produces intent-aware, interpretable captions suitable for planner supervision and safety auditing.

items.title: A Large Language Model-Based Game Equilibrium Selection Approach for Human-Machine Shared Driving
items.topic: A Large Language Model-Based Game Equilibrium Selection Approach for Human-Machine Shared Driving
items.source: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
items.summary: The IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems paper proposes a large language model-based game equilibrium selection approach for human-machine shared driving authority allocation. This approach develops a game equilibrium selection model to seamlessly transition between Stackelberg equilibrium and Nash equilibrium, addressing human-dominated and human-machine equal relationships, respectively. The selection process is based on a large language model that can adapt to different driving scenarios. This research is crucial for human-machine shared driving, as it can improve the effectiveness of shared driving and enhance safety. The proposed approach has the potential to be applied in various autonomous driving scenarios.

items.title: ObsDriveBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Understanding under Adverse Weather with Observability Awareness
items.topic: ObsDriveBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Understanding under Adverse Weather with Observability Awareness
items.summary: The arXiv paper introduces ObsDriveBench, a real-world multi-modal benchmark for adverse-weather autonomous driving, which evaluates vision-language models under real-world adverse weather conditions with multi-modal inputs. ObsDriveBench is designed with three capability dimensions: observability, cross-modal consistency, and scene understanding. The benchmark is essential for evaluating the performance of autonomous driving systems in adverse weather conditions, which is a critical challenge in the development of autonomous vehicles. The ObsDriveBench dataset provides a comprehensive evaluation of vision-language models in adverse weather conditions, enabling the development of more robust autonomous driving systems.
